newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister raps Juppe critics.
newsitem.headline: French minister raps Juppe critics.

text.p: France's Interior Minister on Saturday ticked off members of the ruling centre-right coalition for sniping at unpopular Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre, in a speech to members of Juppe's Gaullist RPR party in Lyon in central France, urged his audience not to help opposition politicians.
"We mustn't give weapons to our opponents by cultivating nuances which very quickly turn into discord," Debre said.

In an interview published on Saturday by the pro-government Le Figaro, sacked finance minister Alain Madelin warned that if the government did not succeed in curing economic woes "the situation could become dangerous given the gap between those who govern and those who are governed".
"On many issues," the outspoken free-marketeer added, "I have ideas which are often very different from Juppe's...To win (1998) general elections, we must win the battle for jobs."

Madelin and former Interior Minister Charles Pasqua among others have criticised Juppe's austerity drive, prompting him to call a vote of confidence which he won on Wednesday in an attempt to rally the ruling centre-right coalition.
Voters' confidence in Juppe has tumbled to an all-time low amid deep gloom about the economy and near-record unemployment, an opinion poll showed on Friday.

The Sofres survey for the weekly Le Figaro Magazine found just 27 percent of those questioned had confidence in conservative Juppe in late September against 34 a month earlier. The numbers lacking confidence rose to 71 percent from 69.
